blockers.title: The closed authenticityCore records returned identifiers, not a defined successful platform attestation
evidence: v19 closes the scheme/payload serialization, makes OS ABI use PATHLESS, and supplies closed pathless subject objects. Those structural repairs reproduce.

The codesign successResult is only that the platform returns exactly one cdhash. No rule requires signature validity, a trusted signing chain, a designated requirement, or another platform trust decision to succeed; authenticityCore retains only the matching cdhash. A trusted capture sensor can faithfully report a cdhash for an object without that equality establishing that the platform trusted it.

The package-db successResult is only that an interface returns one {name, version, digest}. It defines neither package-database membership/verification semantics nor a signature/trust result. 'Package bytes' and 'running-kernel package bytes' have no canonical archive, installed-file collection, membership order, metadata inclusion, or root rule, so two implementations can hash different byte sets while claiming the same scheme.

subjectByScheme names only generic 'trusted platform codesign interface' and 'trusted platform package-db interface' prose, not a concrete per-OS observation/API and verification policy. Its rules apply to pathless OS ABI; mandatory non-pathless loader and framework PLATFORM-ATTESTED events have no corresponding per-scheme operation binding the returned payload and successful trust decision to resolvedObjectIdentity.

unknownOrFailedRefuses is a boolean assertion with no defined success predicate or retained validation result. The actual joins compare signed and observed identifiers field-for-field, so copied or untrusted identifiers can satisfy every explicit equality.
blockers.impact: PLATFORM-ATTESTED can admit an untrusted or differently measured object whose returned label matches the signed core. OS ABI, loader, and framework are mandatory PLATFORM-ATTESTED classes, so G22 cannot derive one reproducible security decision for every required profile and taxonomy cell.
blockers.requiredRepair: For each supported OS and scheme, name the exact platform interface and input object/subject, require and retain the exact successful signature/package trust decision and policy or trust anchor, and bind that result to the same resolved object or running-kernel subject as the observed authenticityCore. Define the canonical package byte collection/root and digest algorithm input. Merely obtaining a cdhash or package tuple must not be success; any invalid, untrusted, unavailable, ambiguous, or mismatched result must refuse.

shouldFix.title: sonameAbi still has contradictory live signed locations and the new signed envelope is not closed
evidence: The new PLATFORM-ATTESTED rules put sonameAbi on a signed-only libc envelope sibling outside authenticityCore and say it is never inside payload. That correctly keeps it out of authenticity equality.

The live identityEvidenceUnion.companions.SONAME-ABI rule still defines the field inside a PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND libc payload and names its role optionalCompanionInsideLibcAuthenticityPayload. loaderTraces.companionObservationShape likewise triggers when the signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED payload carries sonameAbi. Neither rule is historical or aliased to the new sibling location.

No placement can satisfy both 'never inside payload' and 'inside a PLATFORM-ATTESTED payload.' Producers can therefore disagree whether the companion is lawful or whether companionObservation is required.

signedForm permits authenticityCore plus the optional sibling but states extrasRejected only on authenticityCore. It does not reject any other sibling on the signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED envelope, so the claimed two-member envelope remains open even after the core was closed.
shouldFix.impact: A libc entry using the optional metadata has no single conforming encoding, and unknown signed envelope siblings can be silently accepted or rejected by different implementations. Although sonameAbi is metadata-only, the signed schema and required retained companion record remain non-deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Update the canonical companions rule and companionObservationShape to name the signed-only envelope sibling for PLATFORM-ATTESTED while preserving the intended DIGEST-BOUND location. Define the signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED envelope as exactly {authenticityCore, optional sonameAbi for libc}, reject every other sibling, and bind companionObservation to that one signed location.

advisories.title: The resolver's same-resolution association token is not retained as a field
advisories.evidence: v19 correctly removes the impossible path projection and says capturedPath and resolvedObjectIdentity come from the same trusted-sensor resolution. It calls that capture an association token, but resolverObservation requires only capturedPath, canonicalPath, and lookupStepIndex; no unique resolution token or object-handle identity is retained, and lookupStepIndex can repeat across events.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The trusted sensor emits both values in one retained event and the exact canonicalPath/actualOrigin/signedOrigin equality is closed, so the intended same-event association is usable despite lacking an independently named token.
advisories.suggestedRepair: State that the containing event identity is the association token and prohibit cross-event composition, or retain a unique resolutionObservationId/open-object identity shared by capturedPath and resolvedObjectIdentity.
